note.text: Cameroon’s relief includes coastal lowlands, the South Cameroon Plateau, western highlands, the Adamawa Plateau and northern lowlands. Mount Cameroon rises above 4000 m near the coast. The western highlands include mountains and plateaus rather than a uniformly flat surface. Adamawa forms an important elevated zone between wetter southern and drier northern landscapes. A lowland is low relative to surrounding regions, not necessarily below sea level. Relief influences drainage, temperature, rainfall exposure, transport and land use without determining them alone.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to locate broad relief regions and distinguish elevation from relative height and gradient. Builds on: Cameroon’s location and soil-erosion processes. Leads to: drainage divides and the influence of altitude on climate.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Cameroon’s relief includes coastal lowlands, the South Cameroon Plateau, western highlands, the Adamawa Plateau and northern lowlands. Mount Cameroon rises above {4000} m near the coast. The western highlands include mountains and plateaus rather than a uniformly flat surface. Adamawa forms an important elevated zone between wetter southern and drier northern landscapes. A lowland is low relative to surrounding regions, not necessarily below sea level. Relief influences drainage, temperature, rainfall exposure, transport and land use without determining them alone.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Compare the coastal plain around Douala with plateau country around Yaoundé and the western highlands. Greater elevation often brings cooler conditions, while steepness can complicate transport and increase erosion exposure where cover is removed. A high plateau can have locally gentle slopes; altitude and gradient are different properties. The arithmetic uses invented points, not a claimed surveyed summit or valley.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Name the region, describe height and form, then explain one consequence with a qualification. Calculate relative height by subtracting elevations measured from the same datum. Do not interpret a higher point as automatically steeper, safer or more fertile. Exact peak elevations and regional boundaries require the chosen atlas convention.
